Approve. Test-only change that correctly eliminates the random-subnet overlap flake. Verified against the factory and view code: (1) make_RackController(subnet=subnet) routes through make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet, which creates exactly one boot interface with vlan=subnet.vlan (factory.py:1146-1168), so rack.current_config.interface_set.first() deterministically returns the interface on the test subnet (single row, and Interface.Meta.ordering is ("created",) anyway). (2) The rack's AUTO/DISCOVERED links created by the factory are saved with ip="" and are never auto-allocated, so they cannot collide with the discovery IP 10.0.0.1 in by_unknown_ip(), which only excludes discoveries matching non-empty StaticIPAddress.ip values (discovery.py:60-71). (3) The maasserver_discovery view joins subnets on iface.vlan_id = subnet.vlan_id AND neigh.ip << subnet.cidr; since the boot interface is now on subnet.vlan, test_associates_known_subnet and test_is_external_dhcp exercise the identical view path as before (alembic/versions/0004_create_views.py:75-78). The remaining tests that still use make_RackController() without a subnet (e.g. test_does_not_fail_if_cannot_find_subnet) are unaffected because make_Interface places the second interface on a freshly created fabric's VLAN, so the rack's random subnet can never match through the view's VLAN join. No functional or security concerns.

src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.44: Optional maintainability note: this three-line setup (pinned subnet -> rack on subnet -> first interface) is now repeated six times across this file and api/tests/test_discoveries.py. Consider a small helper (e.g. a factory wrapper or a test-class method like make_rack_on_subnet(cidr="10.0.0.0/8")) so future flake fixes of this class only need to touch one place. Non-blocking; the repetition matches existing test style.
